indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B1.4.2.1: Demonstrate knowledge of generation of electricity, its transmission and transformation into other forms of energy
indicator.objective: Know the importance of electricity and identify common household appliances that require electricity to work

skills.description: Identify common household appliances that need electricity to work
Sort items into 'uses electricity' and 'does not use electricity'
Match an appliance to its use
Explain simply why electricity is important

misconceptions: A torch uses electricity from a wall socket.
If an item has a wire, it must use electricity.

questions.stem: Which of these items uses electricity to work?
hints: It gives light when you switch it on.
questions.explanation: An electric bulb uses electricity to give light.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think any item in the house uses electricity.

questions.stem: Which of these does NOT use electricity?
hints: Which one is from the ground?
It is hard and does not need power.
questions.explanation: A stone does not use electricity. It is a natural object.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all objects in the home use electricity.

questions.stem: What do we use an electric iron for?
hints: You use it on a table.
questions.explanation: An electric iron is used to iron clothes and remove creases.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse the iron with a cooking pot.

questions.stem: Why is electricity important in our homes?
hints: Think about a fan or TV.
questions.explanation: Electricity is important because it makes appliances like fans, TVs, and fridges work.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think electricity is only for light.

questions.stem: Which of these is a household appliance that uses electricity?
hints: It is found in the kitchen.
questions.explanation: A fridge is a household appliance that uses electricity to keep food cold.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think vehicles are household appliances.

questions.stem: Which of these uses electricity?
hints: It needs to be plugged in.
questions.explanation: A television uses electricity to show pictures and sound.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think things with screens don't need power.

questions.stem: Which of these does NOT use electricity?
hints: Which one is used for eating?
It does not have a plug.
questions.explanation: A spoon is a simple tool that does not use electricity.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all kitchen items use electricity.

questions.stem: What do we use a fan for?
questions.explanation: A fan uses electricity to spin and give breeze.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a fan produces cold water.

questions.stem: Why do we need electricity in the home?
hints: Think about how many things need a plug.
questions.explanation: We need electricity to power our appliances like lights, TVs, and fridges.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think electricity helps with manual tasks like sweeping.

questions.stem: Kwame wants to keep his food cold. What does he use?
questions.explanation: A fridge uses electricity to keep food cold.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a fan keeps food cold.

questions.stem: Which of these items uses electricity from a battery?
questions.explanation: A torch uses electricity from a battery to give light.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a torch plugs into a wall socket.

questions.stem: Which group has only items that use electricity?
hints: Look for the group where all items need power.
Which group has things that light up or spin?
questions.explanation: A fan, bulb, and TV all use electricity.
questions.misconception: Pupils may include non-electric items in the group.

questions.stem: Why does a television need electricity?
questions.explanation: A television needs electricity to show pictures and produce sound.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a TV works without power.

questions.stem: Ama plugs in her phone to charge. What is she using?
questions.explanation: Ama is using electricity from the socket to charge her phone.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think charging uses water.

questions.stem: What happens to a fan when there is no electricity?
questions.explanation: A fan stops working when there is no electricity because it has no power.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a fan can work without electricity.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT an electrical appliance?
hints: It does not need a plug.
questions.explanation: A bicycle does not use electricity. It is powered by pedaling.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think any machine is an electrical appliance.

questions.stem: Kofi says 'All things in the house use electricity.' Is he right?
options: No, only some things use it
questions.explanation: Kofi is not right. Only some things, like appliances, use electricity. Many things like chairs and cups do not.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all household items are electrical.

questions.stem: Why is it dangerous to touch a socket with wet hands?
options: Water can make electricity shock you
hints: Water and electricity do not mix well.
questions.explanation: Water can conduct electricity, so touching a socket with wet hands can cause a dangerous electric shock.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think water makes electricity safer.

questions.stem: Which of these appliances changes electricity into movement?
questions.explanation: A fan uses electricity to turn its blades, creating movement.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all appliances just produce heat or light.

questions.stem: If there were no electricity, which of these would still work?
hints: Which one is a simple tool?
You use it with your hands.
questions.explanation: A broom does not need electricity. It is a simple tool you use with your hands.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all household tasks require electricity.
